A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EARL study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite reorganization and added analyses.

before.justification: v1 reports original SFT, RL and CoT experiments, benchmark evaluations, qualitative examples and analyses of agreement with human judgments.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds verifier experiments, best-of-five evaluations, complementary image-quality metrics and inference timing measurements.

M1.justification: The Emu3-8B architecture, SFT-to-GRPO recipe, four-component verifier reward, CoT variants and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The smaller-verifier and best-of-five experiments add analyses without replacing the proposed method; vLLM decoding is newly documented implementation information.

E1.justification: The training datasets, six principal evaluation benchmarks and PIEBench are retained. Added verifier correlations use already represented AURORA subtasks; the additional metrics, sampling controls and timing experiments do not establish new data domains or editing tasks.

E2.justification: v1 compares EditAR only on PIEBench. v3 adds this closest autoregressive competitor to the principal six-benchmark VIEScore comparison in Table 2. Table 11 also introduces best-of-five SFT as a comparator for assessing RL against candidate selection.

E3.justification: Original training settings and benchmark subsets are retained, but substantial new evaluation designs are added: a Qwen-7B verifier control, best-of-five inference, CLIP ViT-B/32 and InceptionV3 FID across three retained benchmarks, and timing 50 samples on one A100L GPU. The timing comparison uses 256×256 images except EditAR at 512×512.

E4.justification: v3 adds quantitative verifier–human alignment and a verifier-choice ablation (D.2–D.3), VIEScore component analysis (E.1), complementary CLIP/FID checks (E.2), and best-of-five analysis testing sampling versus policy optimization (E.4). Existing failure examples, fine-grained evaluations and CoT case studies remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. v3 explicitly acknowledges the absence in checklist item 7. Best-of-five sampling is an inference-selection experiment, not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Existing main-table scores, including EARL's 4.80 average, remain unchanged. New results include EditAR's 4.20 average, Qwen-7B-verifier RL at 2.81, best-of-five SFT/RL averages of 4.33/4.83, verifier correlations, CLIP/FID scores and timings. Section 5.3 also corrects the prose CoT average from 2.55 to 3.50, matching the unchanged table.

T1.justification: The SFT loss, GRPO objective, advantage normalization and algorithmic pseudocode match across versions. Relocation and notation corrections do not introduce new mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, listed contributions and conclusion retain their principal claims about RL, complex-edit training and unsuccessful CoT supervision. Section 3 adds an explicit priority claim that EARL is the first RL post-training approach for autoregressive image editing, modestly strengthening novelty positioning.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations attributing gains beyond candidate selection to policy optimization, emphasizing verifier strength, and distinguishing improved edit success from largely preserved perceptual quality. It also discusses training and inference efficiency tradeoffs. Earlier explanations of complex-edit and CoT difficulties, and the substantive limitations, remain.

D1.justification: Appendix F newly documents vLLM-based EARL decoding, training durations and efficiency-measurement resources. Existing hyperparameters, prompt templates and release information are retained. Table 18 lists eight A100L GPUs while F.1 retains the H100 description, creating documentation ambiguity rather than establishing a hardware change.

R1.justification: v3 adds the vLLM/PagedAttention reference and explicitly asserts first use of RL post-training for autoregressive editing. The related-work discussion otherwise retains its scope. Duplicate-reference removal and publication metadata updates do not remove distinct prior works.

P1.justification: v3 tightens setup and results prose, corrects terminology, moves the EARL Recipe box into the introduction, merges background material and groups appendix analyses more systematically. It also appends the NeurIPS checklist. The main narrative and most existing prose remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v3 adds substantial tabular presentations for verifier validation, reward components, CLIP/FID, best-of-five evaluation and compute. Table 2 gains an EditAR row; the existing PIEBench table moves to Appendix E.3, and the human-correlation and action-edit tables are transposed. Existing figures are essentially retained.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens support for the unchanged RL recipe by adding the principal-benchmark EditAR comparison, verifier validation and ablation, and sampling controls that show RL exceeding best-of-five SFT. These address important comparison and attribution gaps in v1, while CLIP/FID broaden quality assessment beyond VIEScore. Continued absence of uncertainty estimates and conflicting new compute descriptions limit precision, but do not outweigh the stronger experimental validation.
